It counts hourly transitions and per-zone dwell ratios, and outputs a thermal preference label (e.g. 'basking-preferred', 'hiding-preferred', 'frequent shuttling'). This skill helps assess whether the environmental temperature gradient is appropriate, infers pet health state (such as abnormal lethargy or stress reaction), and guides keepers to adjust heating layout. Application scenarios: vivariums, breeding tanks, reptile farms. The system monitors continuously, generates daily thermal-zone utilization reports, and pushes reminders when abnormalities occur. Skill features: reptiles are ectotherms that regulate body temperature through behavior. Long-term deviation from normal zone-utilization patterns (e.g. constantly hiding) may indicate disease, parasites, or environmental inadequacy. AI-based automatic monitoring helps keepers catch problems early, optimize setup, and improve animal welfare.
